declarations.docstring: An injective algebra map from a polynomial ring in `n` variables into an integral domain forces `n` to be at most the codomain's transcendence degree.
A base-field algebra map between rational function fields in `n` and `m` variables can exist only when `n ≤ m`.
If a field of transcendence degree `m` contains an injective image of a polynomial ring in `n` variables, then `n ≤ m`.
An injective algebra map from the polynomial ring in `n` variables to the rational function field in `m` variables forces `n ≤ m`.
The rational function field in `m` variables over a field has transcendence degree `m`.
